options.detail: Auto uses the first input filename extension and falls back to YAML for stdin or an unknown extension. Use -p csv for CSV on stdin and add -o to choose the output encoding.
The default is 2. Use --indent 0 for compact JSON. For YAML, 4.44.3 uses four spaces at zero. Version 4.54.3 limits YAML indentation to 2 through 9 spaces and rejects negative input for every format.

forms.grammar: With 4.44.3, YAML zero uses a four-space indent. Positive YAML widths outside 2 through 9 use two spaces. Negative YAML indentation is rejected by the encoder. JSON and XML use no indentation spaces for nonpositive values. This does not promise one-line XML. Other encoders ignore this setting in 4.44.3.

special_values.meaning: For 4.44.3, zero gives four spaces in YAML and no indentation spaces in JSON or XML.

when_absent.meaning: Use 2 spaces for the applicable encoder.

options.summary: Reset YAML styles for block output
options.detail: After evaluating the expression, yq resets styles on the result. Inline maps and lists expand across lines in YAML output.

options.summary: Print a scalar as its raw value
options.detail: A selected YAML string prints without its quotes, color or inline comment. YAML enables this by default. Use --unwrapScalar=false to keep scalar formatting.
Use for plain terminal output. Redirected output is normally plain already. An explicit --colors takes precedence.
Use when an expression also names an existing file. Pass the whole expression as one argument, such as --expression '.items[] | .name'.
